about: TASK-34a7: the clean bench fixture deck (tests/fixtures/bench/clean.json) with a model-style "why" on every quiz answer, as the new prompt asks. Hand-written, not a recording. Used to test that every "why" is stripped on every path, and to measure the output-size cost of the field.
prompt: A 5-question quiz, two flash cards and a short choose-your-path story for pupils aged 8 to 10 on this objective: identify the part played by evaporation and condensation in the water cycle and associate the rate of evaporation with temperature.

elements.content: Water turns into vapour when it gets warm.
Vapour cools and turns back into tiny drops.

elements.label: Tiny drops of water
elements.why: Clouds are vapour that has cooled into tiny water drops.

elements.label: Smoke from fires
elements.why: Pupils see smoke rise and look grey, like a cloud.

elements.label: Dust from roads
elements.why: Pupils know dust floats in air, so think clouds are dust.

elements.label: Snow on hills
elements.why: Clouds sit on hilltops, so pupils link them to the snow there.

elements.content: What makes a puddle dry up faster?

elements.label: A hot sunny day
elements.why: Heat makes water evaporate faster.

elements.label: A cold dark night
elements.why: Pupils mix up drying with the puddle soaking away overnight.

elements.label: A foggy morning
elements.why: Fog looks like water leaving, so pupils think it dries puddles.

elements.label: A frosty week
elements.why: Pupils think ice dries things because frost looks dry.

elements.content: A raindrop lands in a warm pond. What happens next?
The drop rises as vapour and joins a cloud.
The drop rests in the mud until a sunny day.
What falls from clouds when the drops get heavy?

elements.label: Rain
elements.why: Heavy drops fall from clouds as rain.

elements.label: Hail stones
elements.why: Pupils know hail falls from clouds too, but only in cold storms.

elements.label: Fog
elements.why: Fog is cloud near the ground, so pupils think it falls.

elements.label: Steam
elements.why: Pupils mix up the vapour going up with water coming down.

elements.content: Where is most of the water on Earth?

elements.label: In the oceans
elements.why: Oceans hold almost all of Earth's water.

elements.label: In the clouds
elements.why: Clouds look huge, so pupils think they hold the most.

elements.label: In rivers and lakes
elements.why: Rivers and lakes are the water pupils see most often.

elements.label: Under the ground
elements.why: Pupils know wells and springs hold water underground.

elements.content: What happens to water when it freezes?

elements.label: It turns to ice
elements.why: Water freezes into solid ice below 0 °C.

elements.label: It turns to steam
elements.why: Pupils mix up freezing with boiling, the other change of state.

elements.label: It evaporates
elements.why: Pupils think any change makes water go away into the air.

elements.label: It gets lighter
elements.why: Ice floats, so pupils think freezing makes water lighter.
